title: Great Famine kills an estimated 200,000 in Mount Lebanon, roughly half its population
why: Wartime blockade and requisitioning shaped emigration and the memory of the 1920 state's founding generation. (corrected from 'perhaps a third')

title: Greater Lebanon proclaimed, adding Muslim-majority districts
why: Enlarged territory created the sectarian balance that later censuses and quotas argued over.

title: Nationality decree lets Armenian refugees become Lebanese citizens
why: Armenian genocide survivors settled in Beirut camps and Bourj Hammoud and became a permanent parliamentary community.

title: Mohammad Traboulsi wins Lebanon's first Olympic medal, silver in weightlifting
why: Early sporting pride for the young republic at the London Games.
drop_reason: Lebanon won no 1948 medals; first medals 1952; Traboulsi silver was 1972

title: Hassan Bchara takes wrestling silver at Helsinki Olympics
why: A second Olympic medal in the golden-age decade of Lebanese sport.
drop_reason: 1952 silver was Zakaria Chehab; Hassan Bechara won bronze in 1980

title: Baalbeck International Festival opens in the Roman temples
why: Beirut's golden-age cultural showcase, later home to Fairuz and the Rahbani Brothers.

title: Second Pan Arab Games held in Beirut
why: Lebanon hosted the regional games at the height of its open-society image.

title: General Confederation of Lebanese Workers (CGTL) founded
why: The CGTL became the main union body, later unified all licensed unions in 1970.

title: Myrna Bustani becomes the first woman elected to Parliament
why: She won a by-election to her late father's Mount Lebanon seat, a decade after suffrage.

title: All licensed unions converge inside the CGTL
why: Unification produced the labour body that led the 1970s strike waves.

title: CGTL holds a general strike over prices and wages
why: Rising inflation and factory repression pushed the main union into action before the war.

title: Leftist federations call general strike after inflation march
why: Labour unrest in 1974 mixed wage demands with the political polarisation before April 1975.

title: Israel's Litani operation displaces tens of thousands from the south
why: First large Israeli-driven displacement of southern Shia villagers toward Beirut's southern belt.

title: Mountain War displaces large parts of the Chouf Christian population
why: Post-1982 fighting between Druze militias and the Lebanese Forces emptied villages and hardened regional segregation.

title: CGTL general strike over war and economic crisis shakes wartime Lebanon
why: Hyperinflation drove cross-sect union action even as militias ran the country. (corrected from date 1987-05; strike ran 5-10 Nov 1987)

title: CGTL general strike forces Karami government to resign
why: A union strike against inflation toppled a cabinet, the last big labour win before postwar union incorporation.

title: Naturalisation decree grants nationality to a large group of residents
why: Decree 5247 gave citizenship to roughly 150,000 or more, mostly Shia and Sunni residents; counts are contested. (corrected from 1994-06; Hourani gives 157,216 including minors)

title: Bomb kills worshippers at Our Lady of Deliverance church, Zouk Mikael
why: A sectarian attack after the war; the case was later tied to the Lebanese Forces' dissolution.

title: Audiovisual law 382/94 licenses private TV and radio stations
why: Regulated the private broadcasters that carry the sectarian media landscape.

title: Pope John Paul II visits Lebanon and signs apostolic exhortation
why: Reaffirmed Lebanon as a 'message' of coexistence and drew both Christian and Muslim crowds.

title: First municipal elections since 1963
why: Local councils returned after 35 years, reopening a channel for local patronage and quotas.

title: Maronite bishops' statement calls for Syrian army withdrawal
why: A Church-led opening for the sovereignty movement that culminated in 2005.

title: Lebanon hosts the AFC Asian Cup
why: The first major international football tournament after the 2000 Israeli withdrawal.

title: Lebanon's basketball team plays its first FIBA World Championship
why: Basketball became a mass national pastime crossing confessional lines.

title: Beirut Marathon runs for the first time
why: A civil-society-backed mass event presented as a cross-sect public space.

title: Campaign 'My nationality is my right' launched
why: Women's groups began the long push to let mothers pass citizenship, still unmet in 2026.
actors: Collective for Research and Training on Development

title: General strike over fuel and prices ends with protesters shot
why: Army fire killed protesters on the day of a union-led transport and price protest.

title: Journalist and MP Gebran Tueni killed by car bomb
why: Part of the wave of assassinations of critical journalists after Hariri's killing.

title: Raya Haffar El Hassan: first Arab woman finance minister
why: A landmark appointment; she later became interior minister in 2019.

title: Laique Pride secular march calls for civil personal-status law
why: Civil-society campaign against confessional control of marriage and inheritance.

title: Union Coordination Committee leads public-sector strike for new salary scale
why: Teachers and public employees fought five years for a pay scale, reaching Law 46 in 2017.

title: Pope Benedict XVI visits Lebanon
why: The visit called for peace as the Syrian war spilled over and drew crowds of all sects.

title: Interior minister registers Lebanon's first civil marriage
why: A couple removed their sect from state records to marry civilly; a first test of the confessional personal-status system.

title: Twin bombs hit Tripoli mosques
why: Spillover of the Syrian war into Sunni and Alawite Tripoli; one of the deadliest attacks since the civil war.

title: Judge rules homosexuality is not an offence under Article 534
why: A Jdeideh court ruling chipped at the legal basis for prosecutions of LGBT people.

title: Lebanon launches RACE to enrol Syrian children in public schools
why: Afternoon shifts in public schools absorbed hundreds of thousands of Syrian pupils.

title: Lebanon imposes entry and residency rules on Syrians
why: New visa and sponsorship requirements closed the open border and pushed many refugees into irregular status.

title: London conference and the Lebanon Compact tie aid to refugee policy
why: Donor money was linked to work rights and education access for Syrians.

title: Parliament passes Law 46 public-sector salary scale
why: Ended the 2012 UCC strike campaign but was followed by a pension and financing fight. (corrected from 2017-07-21)

title: Parliament repeals Article 522, which let rapists avoid punishment by marriage
why: A feminist campaign win; related articles were repealed later.

title: Arsal evacuation to Idlib begins under Hezbollah-Nusra deal
why: A negotiated return for Syrian fighters and families underlined informal, security-led refugee movement. (corrected from date 2017-08-30 and title 'Arsal returns begin')

title: Parliamentary election sends six women to Parliament
why: Women won 6 of 128 seats after the first proportional vote.

title: Nadine Labaki's Capernaum wins Jury Prize at Cannes
why: Film about Beirut child poverty later became Lebanon's first Oscar-nominated feature for best foreign film.

title: Raya El Hassan becomes first woman interior minister in the Arab world
why: A security portfolio for a woman in Hariri's cabinet; followed by a woman defence minister in 2020.

title: Lebanon orders demolition of concrete Syrian refugee shelters
why: Higher Defence Council decision evicted or pressured tens of thousands in Arsal and elsewhere.

title: Byblos festival drops Mashrou' Leila after religious pressure
why: A flashpoint over the boundary between art, blasphemy and sectarian groups' pressure.

title: Zeina Acar becomes the first woman defence minister in the Arab world
why: She also served as deputy prime minister in the Diab government.

title: Government declares general mobilisation and lockdown against COVID-19
why: Airport, schools and most businesses closed; the first of several pandemic waves.

title: Protesters storm ministries after the port blast
why: Marked the peak of post-blast anger; foreign ministry seized briefly by activists.

title: Macron meets Fairuz in Beirut
why: A cultural moment of national symbolism during the post-blast visit.

title: Parliament passes Law 205 criminalising sexual harassment
why: First explicit sexual-harassment law, after a long NGO campaign.

title: Vaccination campaign starts with first Pfizer doses
why: Initial rollout targeted health workers and the elderly amid platform registration complaints.

title: Medicine shortage empties pharmacy shelves
why: Central-bank subsidy depletion caused shortages of chronic, cancer and baby-formula drugs before subsidies were lifted.

title: Akkar fuel tank explosion kills dozens
why: Fuel shortage and hoarding led to the Tleil disaster, a symbol of the collapse.

title: ESCWA: 74 percent income-poor, 82 percent multidimensionally poor
why: UN agency measure published during the crisis; multidimensional poverty roughly doubled from 42 percent in 2019.

title: Rafik Hariri University Hospital staff escalate strike over pay
why: Public hospital workers' pay was eroded by the lira's collapse.

title: Brevet exam cancelled and schools disrupted by COVID and fuel crisis
why: Two school years of lost days fuelled the flight of teachers and shift to private schools. (title corrected: the Brevet was cancelled in 2021; baccalaureate exams went ahead)

title: Omicron wave drives record daily COVID-19 cases
why: Highest case counts of the pandemic, hospitals again strained.

title: Healthcare workers strike for two days over collapsing salaries
why: Doctors, nurses and paramedics stopped work at public hospitals.

title: Public-sector strike begins as salaries lose value
why: The Lebanese administration was paralysed for long stretches in 2022-23.

title: Government unveils plan to return 15,000 Syrian refugees a month
why: Caretaker Displaced Minister Issam Charafeddine's plan drew UNHCR objections over voluntariness. (corrected from attribution to Bassam Mawlawi and date 2022-07-05)

title: Depositors storm bank branches in armed hold-ups
why: Sali Hafez and others demanded their frozen savings, making bank hold-ups a public cause.

title: Election sends eight women and thirteen reform-camp MPs to Parliament
why: A record number of independents entered Parliament after the 2019 uprising.

title: Cholera outbreak declared over after months of decline
why: Cases fell sharply by early 2023; about 8,000 suspected cases and 23 deaths overall.

title: Security crackdown on Syrian refugees and deportation drive
why: Army and municipalities raided and expelled Syrians, prompting EU and UN concern.

title: Public administration staff begin two-week strike over devalued pay
why: Lira lost about 98 percent of its value, leaving salaries near zero.

title: Public school teachers strike again
why: Teachers demanded payment in dollars or value-indexed pay for basic functioning.

title: Ain al-Hilweh clashes between Fatah and Islamist groups
why: Fighting in the largest Palestinian camp killed at least a dozen and displaced thousands.

title: Reuters videographer Issam Abdallah killed near the southern border
why: Journalists became early casualties of the 2023-24 border war.

title: EU announces one billion euro package for Lebanon
why: Tied to migration control and refugee support, drawing criticism from rights groups.

title: Israeli strike kills three journalists in Hasbaya
why: Journalists staying at a guesthouse were hit in one of several attacks on media in 2024.

title: Israel's Knesset passes law against UNRWA operations
why: The ban, effective in early 2025, threatens services to Palestinians in Lebanon.

title: At least 24 killed as residents try to return to southern villages
why: Israeli forces had not completed withdrawal by the ceasefire deadline, and returnees were fired on.

title: Ziad Rahbani dies
why: The composer and playwright, son of Fairuz, was a generational voice of Lebanese satire and left-wing culture.

title: Disarmament of Palestinian camps begins with handover in Burj al-Barajneh
why: After Hezbollah-era pressure, Fatah began handing over weapons to the Lebanese army.

title: Pope Leo XIV visits Lebanon
why: First papal trip to Lebanon since 2012, with a message of coexistence.

title: Syrian refugee registration grows as UNHCR opens Lebanese registration
why: Open-border arrivals rose through 2012 and no camps were allowed, so refugees scattered into rented rooms and informal tents.

title: Registered Syrian refugees pass half a million
why: The fastest inflow year, preceding the one million mark in April 2014.

title: Engineers request 5-6 emigration certificates a day (UPI)
why: Order of Engineers head Jad Tabet cited daily certificate requests in late 2020.

title: WHO: about 40% of doctors, 30% of nurses gone since 2019
why: A key health-worker flight figure; Order of Physicians counts of roughly 3,000-3,500 doctors and about 5,000 nurses are reported separately.

title: Tripoli protests over lockdown and poverty turn violent
why: Night-time riots in the poorest big city killed one protester and injured hundreds during the January 2021 lockdown.

title: Donors pause UNRWA funding after Israeli allegations
why: The pause hit services for Palestinians in Lebanon, most of whom live in poverty and depend on UNRWA health and schools.

title: Army retirees block roads in Beirut and Tripoli over collapsed pensions
why: Retired servicemen are a recurring protest group since the lira collapse; parliament committees were suspended.

title: Public school teachers hold a warning strike over pay
why: Unions rejected the government's offer with no figures and kept calling for a new pay scale.

title: UN and WHO warn strikes on hospitals hit vulnerable patients
why: During the 2026 war, attacks on hospitals and staff closed wards and cut maternity services.

title: HRW warns of hospital crisis, state debts to hospitals
why: Early warning of the hospital funding squeeze months before the 2020 COVID wave.
